content:
The image shows a corn ear with:
- White fungal mycelium visible growing from the base of the ear over and between kernels
- The ear tip is brown/rotted
- Husks appear bleached/dried prematurely
- Kernels are rotted and shrunken in affected areas
- The white mold growth pattern starts at the base, not the tip

This is the classic presentation of **Diplodia Ear Rot**: white mycelium beginning at the base of the ear, bleached husk appearance, and rotted kernels. Gibberella and Fusarium ear rots typically start at the tip with pink/red mold — not the base with white mold.
